messages:
elaine (acme-data): Hey team, embeddings suddenly started returning 768-d vectors for our billing dataset. We used to get 1536-d ones. No code changes on our side. Anyone seeing that?

jake_support: Hi Elaine — sorry about that. Quick question: are you calling the embeddings endpoint with a model param or relying on default routing?

elaine (acme-data): We're not passing a model. We rely on project defaults. Example request (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_project_XXXX' 
  -H 'X-Project-ID: acme-billing' 
  -d '{"input":"invoice line item"}'
```
We started seeing the smaller dims around 2025-11-12 14:02 UTC.

jake_support: Thanks. Can you paste the token prefix (first 8 chars) in DM? Also, do you have an org-level API key in use anywhere that might override project settings?

elaine (acme-data): Sent the token prefix. We do have an org admin API key but we're not using it in this call.

mahesh_eng: jumping in. I pulled logs for the request id you sent (via DM). I can see route selection picked model "embed-small-alpha" (768d) instead of your expected "embed-large-v2" (1536d). Looks like the routing decision used an org-level mapping for your org id.

elaine (acme-data): But we weren't sending org headers. Why would org mapping apply?

mahesh_eng: There's a subtlety: our internal precedence logic should use project-level config when present, otherwise fall back to org-level defaults. I'm seeing a case where the presence of an org-scoped API key in the account caused the request to be attributed to the org even though the Authorization token is project-scoped. That attribution path misrouted model selection.

jake_support: Repro steps so we can escalate:
1) Create org key + project key in same account.
2) Make embeddings call with project key but also include header `X-Org-ID` (some SDKs add this automatically) or have org key present in account.
3) Server routing resolves to org mapping and picks the smaller model.

nina_devex: Noted. We should advise customers to explicitly pass `model: "embed-large-v2"` as a short-term mitigation. Also our SDKs will want to avoid auto-injecting org headers.

elaine (acme-data): Workaround applied, sending model param now and dims back to 1536. Thanks. But this will break a bunch of existing clients if we don't fix routing.

mahesh_eng: Agreed. I reproduced locally with two keys. Minimal repro:
```bash
# org key created with default model embed-small-alpha
ORIG_KEY=sk_org_YYYYYYYY
# project key expecting embed-large-v2
PRJ_KEY=sk_proj_ZZZZZZZZ
# request with project key but local account also has org key configured
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PRJ_KEY" \n  -H "X-Org-ID: org-acme" \n  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
Response shows 768-d vector and model header `x-selected-model: embed-small-alpha`.

mahesh_eng: Root cause: attribution logic checks for org membership by matching tokens against account store. If any org-level key exists and we resolve an org id from headers or token metadata, we set routing context to org before loading project config. We missed a clause to prefer explicit Authorization token's project scope when present.

jake_support: Severity? Customer impact: multiple customers that created org keys then migrated to project keys could be affected.

mahesh_eng: I'd call it P1 for correctness of model selection (dims / schema mismatch). I've added a quick guard in local branch to prefer token-scoped project mappings when Authorization token is project-scoped.

nina_devex: Can we push a hotfix? Also we need a safe fallback: when mismatch between selected model dims and expected dims from project config, reject the request with a helpful error instead of returning wrong-dimension vectors. That would surface the issue to integration tests.

mahesh_eng: Agreed. Plan:
- Hotfix routing precedence (short-term) : patch and rollout within 2 hours.
- Add a validation step: if selected-model.dim != project.expected_dim then log error and (configurable) either reject or return a warning header.
- Postmortem + docs update about header precedence and SDK changes.

infra-bot: deploy-bot started rolling hotfix to canary cluster at 1765556120

jake_support: I'll email affected customers and open a support bulletin. @mahesh can you add the failing request ids to the internal ticket? Ticket RED-3129 opened.

elaine (acme-data): Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll keep explicit model param for now until you confirm the rollout. :+1:

mahesh_eng: Canary looks good (no regressions). Rolling to prod in 10m.

infra-bot: deploy-bot finished rollout to prod at 1765557430 — no alerts fired.

nina_devex: Docs PR created describing header precedence and recommended best practices (explicit model param if you have org/project keys). Link: https://git.redwood/docs/embed-routing-precedence (internal). :rocket:

jake_support: Closing the immediate escalation. Remaining action items: postmortem, validation step, SDK patch to stop auto-injecting `X-Org-ID`.

elaine (acme-data): Confirmed correct vectors after rollout. Thank you! :eyes:
